items.description: R1 — "`backup.yml` delivers the staged secret_id on `stat.exists` alone, never checking it against the live role. The staging dir is a persistent per-checkout `tmp/`, so one stale file installs a dead credential permanently." Resolved: before a staged backup secret_id is installed on the OpenBao nodes, the run checks it against the live `backup` AppRole, and a dead one fails the run with a message naming `openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true` (today the delivery at ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/backup.yml:92-100 is gated on `_openbao_staged_secret_id.stat.exists` alone).
items.rationale: The login-before-install mechanism is implemented and confirmed working live against the real prd `backup` AppRole. `backup.yml` gates delivery on `_openbao_backup_secret_id_proven` (a real HTTP 200 from the staged role_id/secret_id login), and a 400 response fails the run naming `-e openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true` before any file is copied. This pass ran `ansible-playbook site-openbao.yml --tags openbao_backup --check` against the real srvvault1-3 fleet: the staged credentials in this checkout's `tmp/` logged in successfully (HTTP 200) against the live backup AppRole on all three nodes, proving the check makes a real, meaningful call against the live role exactly as designed (it then failed at the separate revoke-self step — see V02, a different, already-tracked gap). The dead-secret_id (HTTP 400) and delivery paths were proven in P1's harness against a real OpenBao 2.5.4 dev server (plan.md P1 Record).

ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/backup.yml:82-92 — 400 fails naming -e openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true, before any copy task
ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/backup.yml:174-193 — delivery of role_id/secret_id gated on the proven or already-installed secret_id

Live 2026-09-14: `cd ansible && cexec iac poetry run ansible-playbook playbooks/site-openbao.yml --tags openbao_backup --check` — task "Log in with the staged backup AppRole credentials" -> ok on srvvault1/2/3 (real 200 from the live backup AppRole)

items.description: There is no silent skip and no automatic re-mint. Each node's own pass installs a staged secret_id only after an AppRole login with the staged role_id and secret_id succeeds; no admin token is needed. A rejected login fails the run, naming `openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true`. The check mints no secret_id, revokes or deletes no credential, and leaves no lasting login token behind. Minting stays behind the operator's `openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true` (default false, ansible/roles/openbao/defaults/main.yml:87).
items.rationale: The code correctly never installs a secret_id without a successful proving login and mints/revokes nothing extra (confirmed by reading and by P1's harness: 'a secret_id survives repeated logins', 'nothing under roles/openbao/ sets secret_id_num_uses'). But 'no lasting login token behind' does not currently hold on the live cluster: this pass's live run (see V01) proved the login (200), then the self-revoke failed with HTTP 403 permission denied, because the backup-policy currently deployed on prd predates P1's `auth/token/revoke-self` grant (already tracked as close-out N1/B1, not a new finding). The proving login's token was therefore left un-revoked in real prd OpenBao this pass — no worse than a normal nightly backup run's token (the wrapper itself never revokes its token either; both expire on their default TTL). The run correctly failed loudly rather than silently continuing. This settles itself on the first plain (non-rotation) `site-openbao.yml` apply: each host's own policy-write task (approle.yml, which runs before backup.yml) rewrites the backup policy to include the grant before that host's own proving login runs, per P6's Record ('it also rewrites any policy whose text differs, which covers P1's revoke-self grant for a snapshot taken before it').
evidence: ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/backup.yml:106-129 — the self-revoke and its fail task
ansible/roles/openbao/templates/backup-policy.hcl.j2:10-14 — the revoke-self grant this slice added
Live 2026-09-14: same run as V01 — "Fail when the proving login's token was not revoked" -> fatal on srvvault1/2/3, HTTP 403 permission denied (currently-deployed policy predates the grant)
close-out.md N1/B1 — this exact consequence already flagged by the phase reviewer

Owed: a plain `cd ansible && cexec iac poetry run ansible-playbook playbooks/site-openbao.yml` apply (no flags needed — the staged secret_id already logs in live) settles it fleet-wide on the first pass, each host healing its own policy before its own proving login

items.description: The remedy the failure names works. A `site-openbao.yml -e openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true` run from the checkout holding the dead staged secret_id completes on the serialized apply (ansible/playbooks/site-openbao.yml:171): the bootstrap host's pass re-stages a fresh secret_id, and every node's pass, the later ones included, proves it by login. The run leaves every OpenBao node holding a secret_id the live `backup` AppRole accepts. Proving this live takes a rotation run, which mints a fresh never-expiring secret_id for all six AppRoles and revokes none of the old ones (ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/approle.yml:329-347). The test phase names that cost and leaves the run to the operator; it does not present the run as a routine proof.
items.rationale: Per the plan's own instruction, proving this live takes a deliberate rotation run (mints a fresh never-expiring secret_id for all six AppRoles, revokes none of the old) and the test phase is directed to name that cost rather than run it routinely. Not attempted this pass.

items.description: R2 — "Every leg of the wrapper is a bare `curl -fsS`, so a failure never says which call broke. Cost three months of misdiagnosis." Resolved: every call the backup wrapper makes — leader check, AppRole login, snapshot, policy list and reads, KV walk and reads, auth and mount reads, upload (ansible/roles/openbao/templates/openbao-backup.sh.j2:29, :38-44, :46, :52-53, :57-58, :73-82, :102-103, :117-122) — names itself on failure, with the HTTP status and, for OpenBao calls, OpenBao's error text.
items.rationale: Read the shipped template: every OpenBao and upload call goes through the request/bao_request/bao_api/bao_check helpers, which name the call (method+path or 'POST <url>/upload'), the HTTP status, and (for OpenBao calls) the collapsed 'errors' text from the JSON body. Functionally proven in P2's 18-case harness against a real OpenBao 2.5.4 server (raft storage) plus Python mocks, covering every named leg: leader check, login, snapshot, policy LIST/read, KV walk/read, sys/auth, sys/mounts, and the upload (401 plain text, unreachable, TLS mismatch, non-JSON 502, truncated body). Not run against real prd OpenBao this pass (that means triggering a real backup run with root/admin privileges on a live node, out of scope for a read-only test pass).
evidence: ansible/roles/openbao/templates/openbao-backup.sh.j2:37-73 — request/bao_request/bao_check/bao_api
ansible/roles/openbao/templates/openbao-backup.sh.j2:156-164 — the upload's failure line
plan.md P2 Record — 18/18 cases pass against real OpenBao 2.5.4 + Python mocks, covering every named leg

items.rationale: The mechanism is implemented and functionally proven off-host (P3's r2 harness imported the real roles/microk8s/handlers/main.yml into a scratch play and notified all three names under --check: each announcement fired changed on both hosts and the real handler was skipped, recap changed=4 skipped=3). This pass's own live --check of renew-internal-tls.yml against real prd hosts (which shares this same handlers file via import_role) ran clean with changed=0 and no announcements, consistent with a converged fleet, but did not exercise a host with real pending drift to see the announcement fire on prd. As the plan itself states, that needs the operator's site-k8s.yml --check --diff against a node with a pending notifier change.

Resolved: the kubelite restart waits for readiness — the API server's readiness check on control-plane nodes, the node's Ready state on workers (or, if that proves impractical inside the single throttled restart step, the kubelet health check with the handler comment saying so) — within `microk8s_kubelite_ready_timeout` (ansible/roles/microk8s/defaults/main.yml:256; today's probe selection at ansible/roles/microk8s/handlers/main.yml:72-75).
items.rationale: The readiness-detection logic itself was validated read-only against real prd hosts during planning (srvk8s1 and srvk8s4 probes matched), and the wait's control flow passed an 8-scenario stub harness, but no actual kubelite restart has been triggered against a real apiserver node or worker to see the wait behave end-to-end. That needs an operator-triggered restart.
